text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and other developers. Good naming conventions matter a lot: choose clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Keep functions small and focused on one task, because short functions are simpler to test and reuse. Finally, remember that clean code is much easier to maintain. When you return to your project months later, readable code saves you time and prevents mistakes. In short, writing clean code from the start is always a smart investment.
